scenes.tts: Two hindbrain segments look almost alike. One builds the neurons that work the jaw. Another builds those that move the face. What tells them apart?
scenes.visual: Title card: Two Segments, Two Jobs. Two identical bulges of an embryonic hindbrain; one glows toward a jaw outline, the other toward a face outline. A question mark between them.
scenes.narration: Two hindbrain segments look almost alike. One builds the neurons that work the jaw. Another builds those that move the face. What tells them apart?

scenes.tts: From above, the early hindbrain is a row of bulges called rhombomeres. They run from r one to r seven, front to back.
scenes.caption: From above, the early hindbrain is a row of bulges called rhombomeres. They run from r1 to r7, front to back.
scenes.visual: Dorsal view of the hindbrain, anterior at left, between midbrain and spinal cord. Bulges draw in one by one, labelled r1 to r7, with a fainter r8 behind.
scenes.narration: From above, the early hindbrain is a row of bulges called rhombomeres. They run from r1 to r7, front to back.

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty-nine, Andrew Lumsden and Roger Keynes mapped where these motor neurons arise, in chick embryos.
scenes.caption: In 1989, Andrew Lumsden and Roger Keynes mapped where these motor neurons arise, in chick embryos.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Lumsden and Keynes, 1989, chick embryo. Outlines of jaw, face and throat muscles beside the hindbrain.
scenes.narration: In 1989, Andrew Lumsden and Roger Keynes mapped where these motor neurons arise, in chick embryos.

scenes.tts: Trigeminal neurons, for jaw muscles, came from r two and r three. Facial neurons came from r four and r five.
scenes.caption: Trigeminal neurons, for jaw muscles, came from r2 and r3. Facial neurons came from r4 and r5.
scenes.visual: r2 and r3 fill with one colour labelled V, first-arch (jaw) muscles; r4 and r5 fill with a second colour labelled VII, second-arch muscles. Small note: in mammals, these second-arch neurons move the face.
scenes.narration: Trigeminal neurons, for jaw muscles, came from r2 and r3. Facial neurons came from r4 and r5.

scenes.tts: Swallowing neurons came from r six and r seven.
scenes.caption: Swallowing neurons came from r6 and r7.
scenes.visual: r6 and r7 fill with a third colour labelled IX, glossopharyngeal, swallowing. Gold exit stubs appear at r2, r4 and r6.
scenes.narration: Swallowing neurons came from r6 and r7.

scenes.tts: Are the bulges real units? Predict. Label one cell before boundaries appear, and one after. Where do their descendants go?
scenes.visual: Question card over the hindbrain row: one gold cell marked before boundaries, one marked after. Where do their descendants go?
scenes.narration: Are the bulges real units? Predict. Label one cell before boundaries appear, and one after. Where do their descendants go?

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety, Scott Fraser, Keynes and Lumsden did it with a tracer dye. Clones labelled early could span two rhombomeres. Clones labelled after boundaries formed stayed inside one.
scenes.caption: In 1990, Scott Fraser, Keynes and Lumsden did it with a tracer dye. Clones labelled early could span two rhombomeres. Clones labelled after boundaries formed stayed inside one.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Fraser, Keynes and Lumsden, 1990. Panel one: gold descendants spill across the r3/r4 boundary. Panel two: gold descendants stay within r3.
scenes.narration: In 1990, Scott Fraser, Keynes and Lumsden did it with a tracer dye. Clones labelled early could span two rhombomeres. Clones labelled after boundaries formed stayed inside one.

scenes.tts: Each rhombomere is a compartment: its progenitors do not cross into the next. Some neurons born later still migrate across.
scenes.visual: Each rhombomere outlined as a closed block, labelled compartment. One later-born neuron crosses a boundary, labelled later neurons can migrate.
scenes.narration: Each rhombomere is a compartment: its progenitors do not cross into the next. Some neurons born later still migrate across.

scenes.tts: Units that keep their cells need a label: a set of transcription factors, mostly from Hox genes.
scenes.visual: Each rhombomere gets an empty tag. The words transcription factors and Hox genes appear above the row.
scenes.narration: Units that keep their cells need a label: a set of transcription factors, mostly from Hox genes.

scenes.tts: In mouse, Hox domains have front edges at rhombomere boundaries. Read the code column by column. Every rhombomere differs.
scenes.visual: A rhombomere-by-gene grid builds column by column, r1 to r7, with dots for Hoxa2, Hoxb2, Hoxb1, Hoxa3 and Hoxb3, Hoxb4 and Hoxd4, Krox20 and MafB. Label: simplified early mouse code; levels and later changes left out.
scenes.narration: In mouse, Hox domains have front edges at rhombomere boundaries. Read the code column by column. Every rhombomere differs.

scenes.tts: Rhombomeres r three and r four share Hox A two and Hox B two. What separates them is Krox twenty in r three. And later, strong Hox B one in r four.
scenes.caption: Rhombomeres r3 and r4 share Hoxa2 and Hoxb2. What separates them is Krox20 in r3. And later, strong Hoxb1 in r4.
scenes.visual: Columns r3 and r4 highlighted; Hoxa2 and Hoxb2 glow in both. Then the Krox20 dot in r3 and the strong Hoxb1 dot in r4 light up.
scenes.narration: Rhombomeres r3 and r4 share Hoxa2 and Hoxb2. What separates them is Krox20 in r3. And later, strong Hoxb1 in r4.

scenes.tts: One idea to carry through: more early retinoic acid, a more posterior code; the code helps set the neurons.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: More early retinoic acid, a more posterior code; the code helps set the neurons.
scenes.narration: One idea to carry through: more early retinoic acid, a more posterior code; the code helps set the neurons.

scenes.tts: Early in the hindbrain, more retinoic acid, a vitamin A product, pushes a segment toward a more posterior identity.
scenes.visual: The card adds: more early retinoic acid, a vitamin A product, means a code like that of segments farther back. Small print: a direction, not a count of Hox genes. Shading from pale at the front to dark at the back appears under the row, labelled: schematic, not a measured profile.
scenes.narration: Early in the hindbrain, more retinoic acid, a vitamin A product, pushes a segment toward a more posterior identity.

scenes.tts: That combination, sharpened by segment genes such as Krox twenty, helps decide which motor neurons it builds.
scenes.caption: That combination, sharpened by segment genes such as Krox20, helps decide which motor neurons it builds.
scenes.visual: The card adds: sharpened by segment genes such as Krox20; helps decide which motor neurons.
scenes.narration: That combination, sharpened by segment genes such as Krox20, helps decide which motor neurons it builds.

scenes.tts: So lookalike segments are not alike. Each carries its own code.
scenes.visual: Closing card: lookalike segments, different codes, different neurons.
scenes.narration: So lookalike segments are not alike. Each carries its own code.
